name: Context Isolation via Sub-Agents
description: Experiment with spawning fresh Claude sessions for story execution to prevent context degradation. GSD's core insight is that Claude quality degrades as context fills ('context rot'). Their solution: each executor gets an isolated 200k-token window. This ENH explores whether FADE can benefit from similar isolation.

userStories.title: Research context rot in FADE sessions
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to understand if/when context rot affects FADE sessions so we can decide if isolation is needed
acceptanceCriteria: Document typical context size after N stories (measure with real PRDs)
Identify at what context size quality noticeably degrades
Compare output quality: story 1 vs story 5 vs story 10 in same session
Document findings in learned.md or spike output

userStories.title: Design isolation architecture
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a design doc for how sub-agent isolation would work in FADE
acceptanceCriteria: Document how parent orchestrator would spawn child executors
Define what context each executor receives (PRD, FADE.md, relevant files)
Define how executor reports completion back to orchestrator
Address: how does learned.md propagate between sessions?
Address: how are git commits coordinated across executors?
Output is a design doc, not implementation

userStories.title: Prototype isolated story execution
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a minimal prototype of spawning a fresh Claude session per story
acceptanceCriteria: fade run --isolated flag triggers new execution mode
Each story spawns: claude --print with story-specific context
Context includes: FADE.md, current story from PRD, relevant standards
Context excludes: progress.md history, previous story details
Prototype can execute single story, report success/failure

userStories.title: Compare isolated vs continuous execution
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to compare quality and speed of isolated vs continuous modes
acceptanceCriteria: Run same PRD (5+ stories) in both modes
Measure: total time, token usage, output quality
Quality assessment: code correctness, test pass rate, style consistency
Document trade-offs: isolation overhead vs context rot prevention
Make recommendation: default mode, when to use each

userStories.title: Learned.md synchronization
userStories.description: As a developer using isolated mode, I want learnings from each story to be available to subsequent stories
acceptanceCriteria: After each isolated story completes, orchestrator reads its learned.md additions
Learnings are injected into context for next story
Handles case where executor adds to learned.md mid-story
Learnings persist even if session is interrupted

technicalNotes.gsdApproach: GSD spawns 'executors' with fresh 200k windows. They can run in parallel when tasks are independent.
technicalNotes.fadeConstraint: FADE is serial by design (one story at a time). Isolation benefits us for long PRDs, not parallelism.
technicalNotes.implementation: Could use claude --print with context file, or explore Claude Code's Task tool for sub-agents.
technicalNotes.riskOfOverengineering: This may not be needed if FADE's checkpoint-and-restart pattern already mitigates context rot. US-001 should determine if this is a real problem before building solutions.
technicalNotes.spikeFirst: Consider making this a SPIKE type PRD if US-001 reveals context rot isn't a significant issue.
